comments.comment: At 34:01, I completely agree with this. I was bullied a lot as a kid, and my way of dealing with it was to laugh it off. It made the pain less intense and the bullying seem less severe. I remember once a girl at school told me, 'You know, they talk about you behind your back.' My response was, 'Then I know I'll never be forgotten,' and that was it. I never heard anything about it again and I didn't really care. As long as they didn’t say it to my face, they could say whatever they wanted; I didn’t care then and I still don't. Your opinions are yours, and if you don't like me, that's fine – just don't talk to me, and we'll be fine. But you need some bullying and some trauma in your life to build the right defenses against negative opinions. Otherwise, you end up crying over everything that goes against your opinion and just become entitled and a 'Karen.'  The hardest trauma I’m going through right now is losing my dad. I hope it gets better, but I’m not feeling it does. It’s really hard. My dad and I had the strongest bond. We were always there for each other. I lived with my dad most of my life, all the way into my 30s. I took care of my dad when he became weak, doing everything for him like he did for me as a kid. When he passed away on September 13, 2023, my world crumbled. That was the first time I felt real heartbreak. Now, I’m slowly trying to pick up the pieces and change my life by 120%. I wouldn't say I'm lost because I would do it all over again for my love for my dad. But for the last five years, I didn’t really have a life because I had to take care of my dad plus maintain a full-time job. Now, I am trying to get that back. So, besides my world collapsing, I now have all this stuff dumped on me that I have to fix, and I’m stressed out. But I’m a fighter and I’m dealing with it. As they say, no matter the storm, there's always light at the end of it.  Anyway, I just want to clarify that if you've been in bad places and traumatic situations, then you get used to it. It doesn’t really affect you the same later in life. It makes it easier to see things for what they are instead of being upset over them.
